verses.text: Moses finished setting up the Holy Tent. He anointed it and made it holy, with all its furniture, and he anointed the altar and all its tools and made them holy.
On that day the leaders of Israel brought gifts. These were the heads of the family groups, the leaders of the tribes who had been in charge of the counting.
They brought their gifts to the LORD: six covered wagons and twelve oxen, one wagon for every two leaders and an ox from each one. They brought them in front of the Holy Tent.
The LORD said to Moses,
"Accept these gifts from them, so they can be used for the work at the Tent of Meeting. Give them to the Levites, to each group as their work needs."
So Moses took the wagons and the oxen and gave them to the Levites.
He gave two wagons and four oxen to the Gershonites, as their work needed,
and four wagons and eight oxen to the Merarites, as their work needed. They worked under the direction of Ithamar, son of Aaron the priest.
But Moses gave none to the Kohathites, because they were in charge of the holy things, which had to be carried on their shoulders.
When the altar was anointed, the leaders brought gifts to dedicate it, and they presented their gifts in front of the altar.
The LORD said to Moses, "Each day, one leader must bring his gift for the dedication of the altar."
On the first day, Nahshon son of Amminadab, from the tribe of Judah, brought his gift.

His gift was one silver plate weighing one hundred thirty shekels, and one silver bowl weighing seventy shekels, by the official weight of the holy place. Both were full of fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering.
He also brought one gold dish weighing ten shekels, full of incense,
one young bull, one ram, and one one-year-old male lamb for a burnt offering,
one male goat for a sin offering,
and for the peace offering, two oxen, five rams, five male goats, and five one-year-old male lambs. This was the gift of Nahshon son of Amminadab.
On the second day, Nethanel son of Zuar, the leader of Issachar, brought his gift.

He also brought one gold dish weighing ten shekels, full of incense,

These were the gifts from the leaders of Israel to dedicate the altar when it was anointed: twelve silver plates, twelve silver bowls, and twelve gold dishes.
Each silver plate weighed one hundred thirty shekels, and each bowl seventy. All the silver dishes together weighed two thousand four hundred shekels, by the official weight of the holy place.
The twelve gold dishes full of incense weighed ten shekels each, by the official weight of the holy place. All the gold dishes together weighed one hundred twenty shekels.
The animals for the burnt offering were twelve young bulls, twelve rams, and twelve one-year-old male lambs, with their grain offerings. Twelve male goats were given for the sin offering.
The animals for the peace offering were twenty-four bulls, sixty rams, sixty male goats, and sixty one-year-old male lambs. These were the gifts for dedicating the altar after it was anointed.

When Moses went into the Tent of Meeting to speak with the LORD, he heard the voice speaking to him from above the cover on the Covenant Box, from between the two winged creatures. In this way the LORD spoke to him.
